evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.9.2: in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus
Sen. Ep. 123.1: in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī
terms.comment: With ad or in and the accusative; towns and domum take the accusative alone, as after every verb of motion.

phrases.latin: itinere cōnfectus incommodō magis quam longō in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē
phrases.english: worn out by a journey more awkward than long, I got to my place at Alba late at night: nothing is ready but me

phrases.latin: inde austrō lēnissimō caelō serēnō nocte illā et diē posterō in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus
phrases.english: from there, with the gentlest of south winds and a clear sky, that night and the next day we got to Italy at Hydruntum, enjoying ourselves all the way

sources: Lewis & Short: pervenio
